deities: Mayuranathar (Mayuranathaswami — Shiva, swayambhu lingam facing west)
festivals: Aippasi Thula Snanam (holy bath in the Cauvery at the Thula Ghat, October-November; includes Mudavan Muzhukku)

history.dynasty: Chola — stone temple attributed to Queen Sembiyan Mahadevi; later renovations by Pallava, Chola, Pandya and Vijayanagara rulers (inscriptions of Parantaka Chola, Kulothunga III, Rajaraja III and Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan recorded)
history.period: Medieval (origins claimed 7th century; stone construction 9th-13th century)
history.summary: Mayuranathaswami Temple in the heart of Mayiladuthurai is the town's presiding Shiva temple and one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, praised in the Tevaram hymns of Appar, Sundarar and Sambandar (and sung by Manickavasagar and Arunagirinathar). History: claimed 7th-century origins; the stone temple was built by Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi with later additions by subsequent dynasties — about 17 inscriptions (recorded by ASI in 1907, 1911) document royal donors. The nine-tier Rajagopuram, Tridala Vimanam and spacious granite prakarams date from these periods; exact dating of the structures is unverified. Legend: Goddess Parvati, cursed to be born as a peahen (mayil), worshipped Shiva here in penance and was freed; Shiva then took the name Mayuranathar and the town Mayiladuthurai. Notables: the swayambhu lingam faces west; Agasthya (Chandana) Vinayaka said to have emerged from a sandalwood tree; Jwala Shani (Saturn with a ring of fire — rare); Nataraja in Mayura Tandava; the Nandi in mid-Cauvery; and the Mudavan Muzhukku story (the bath extended a day for a lame devotee). Timing conflicts across sources (5:00/5:30/6:00 AM opening; evening close 8:30/9:00 PM) — verify locally.

name: Mayuranathaswami Temple
town_description: Mayiladuthurai (formerly Mayavaram) is a town in Mayiladuthurai district on the southern bank of the river Cauvery, in the Kaveri delta. The temple stands in the heart of the town, and the Thula Ghat on the Cauvery is nearby.

travel.railway: Mayiladuthurai Junction — about 1 km from the temple (verify).
travel.road: On the Chidambaram-Thanjavur highway; about 70 km from Thanjavur and 120 km from Tiruchirappalli; well connected by state buses.

visitor_information.best_time: October-November (Aippasi) for Thula Snanam — the most auspicious bathing season; October to March for pleasant weather.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM to 12:00 PM; 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM (verify locally; sources report 5:00-12:00 and 4:00-8:30 variants). Entry free.
